mcqs.question: What does the term “tetravalent” mean when describing a carbon atom?

options.A: It can form four covalent bonds with other atoms
options.B: It can form two covalent bonds with other atoms
options.C: It can form only single bonds and no multiple bonds
options.D: It can form five covalent bonds with other atoms

mcqs.answer: It can form four covalent bonds with other atoms
mcqs.explanation: Carbon has four valence electrons, so it can share each of them to form four covalent bonds. This tetravalency is the basis for the vast number of carbon‑containing molecules. Options B and D give incorrect numbers of bonds, and C incorrectly limits carbon to only single bonds.

mcqs.question: Which statement best illustrates the catenation property of carbon?

options.A: Carbon atoms can link together to form long chains or rings
options.B: Carbon readily forms ionic bonds with metals
options.C: Carbon exists only as carbon dioxide in the atmosphere
options.D: Carbon forms a double bond only with oxygen

mcqs.answer: Carbon atoms can link together to form long chains or rings
mcqs.explanation: Catenation refers to the ability of an element to bond to itself, producing chains, branched structures, or rings. Carbon’s strong C–C bond makes this possible. The other options describe ionic bonding, a specific compound, or a particular bond type, none of which represent catenation.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an organic compound?
mcqs.explanation: Organic compounds are defined as compounds containing carbon–hydrogen (C–H) bonds. Methane has one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms, satisfying this definition. NaCl is an inorganic salt, H₂O contains no carbon, and CO₂, although containing carbon, lacks C–H bonds and is classified as inorganic in the NCERT context.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise structural diversity of carbon compounds
mcqs.question: A chemist studies three compounds: (i) CH₄, (ii) C₂H₄, and (iii) C₆H₆. Which statement correctly reflects the structural diversity shown by these molecules?

options.A: All three have the same type of carbon‑carbon bonding
options.B: They illustrate single, double, and aromatic carbon‑carbon bonding respectively
options.C: All are saturated hydrocarbons with only single bonds
options.D: They all possess identical molecular formulas

mcqs.answer: They illustrate single, double, and aromatic carbon‑carbon bonding respectively
mcqs.explanation: CH₄ contains only single C–C (none) and C–H bonds (a saturated molecule). C₂H₄ has a carbon‑carbon double bond, representing unsaturation. C₆H₆ (benzene) has a delocalised aromatic system, a distinct type of bonding. Thus the three together demonstrate single, double, and aromatic bonding diversity. Options A, C, and D are incorrect for the reasons stated.

mcqs.question: A student claims that carbon can form five covalent bonds because it can expand its octet. Which of the following statements correctly refutes this misconception?

options.A: Carbon can form a maximum of four covalent bonds because it has only four valence electrons
options.B: Carbon frequently forms five bonds in compounds like CO₂
options.C: Carbon’s d‑orbitals allow it to accommodate extra bonds
options.D: Carbon can expand its octet in the presence of highly electronegative atoms

mcqs.answer: Carbon can form a maximum of four covalent bonds because it has only four valence electrons
mcqs.explanation: Carbon’s ground‑state electron configuration (2s²2p²) provides four valence electrons, allowing at most four covalent bonds. It cannot expand its octet because it lacks low‑energy d‑orbitals. Options B, C, and D are factually incorrect and perpetuate the misconception.

mcqs.question: Why does carbon exhibit far more extensive catenation than silicon, even though both are in Group 14?

options.A: The C–C bond energy is significantly higher than the Si–Si bond energy
options.B: Carbon has a larger atomic radius than silicon, facilitating chain formation
options.C: Silicon is more electronegative than carbon, preventing self‑bonding
options.D: Carbon forms ionic bonds with itself, which are stronger than covalent Si–Si bonds

mcqs.answer: The C–C bond energy is significantly higher than the Si–Si bond energy
mcqs.explanation: C–C bonds (~348 kJ mol⁻¹) are much stronger than Si–Si bonds (~226 kJ mol⁻¹), making carbon chains more stable. The larger atomic radius of silicon actually weakens Si–Si bonding, and electronegativity differences do not favor silicon catenation. Carbon does not form ionic bonds with itself.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly distinguishes an organic compound from an inorganic one?

options.A: Methanol (CH₃OH) – an organic compound; Sodium chloride (NaCl) – an inorganic compound
options.B: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) – an organic compound; Methane (CH₄) – an inorganic compound
options.C: Water (H₂O) – an organic compound; Benzene (C₆H₆) – an inorganic compound
options.D: Ammonia (NH₃) – an organic compound; Glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) – an inorganic compound

mcqs.answer: Methanol (CH₃OH) – an organic compound; Sodium chloride (NaCl) – an inorganic compound
mcqs.explanation: Organic compounds contain carbon‑hydrogen (C–H) bonds; methanol has such bonds, while NaCl contains no carbon. CO₂, H₂O, and NH₃ lack C–H bonds and are classified as inorganic in the NCERT syllabus, whereas benzene and glucose are organic. Hence only option A correctly separates an organic from an inorganic substance.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise structural diversity of carbon compounds
mcqs.question: In a competitive exam, which of the following statements about the structural diversity of carbon is NOT correct?

options.A: Carbon can form straight chains, branched chains, and cyclic structures
options.B: Carbon cannot form multiple bonds with itself
options.C: Carbon exhibits structural isomerism due to its ability to bond in different ways
options.D: Carbon can be part of heteroatom‑containing compounds such as alcohols and amines

mcqs.answer: Carbon cannot form multiple bonds with itself
mcqs.explanation: Carbon readily forms multiple (double and triple) bonds with other carbon atoms, as seen in alkenes, alkynes, and aromatic compounds. Therefore statement B is false. Statements A, C, and D correctly describe carbon’s versatility: chain and ring formation, isomerism, and inclusion in functional groups containing heteroatoms.
